item.title: EU defends measures to close ‘loopholes’ in carbon border tax
item.description: The EU defends temporary carbon border tax exemption for fertilisers for farmers — while tightening the levy on steel and aluminium-heavy products.

item.title: Threat of ‘tactical’ Russian nuclear strike in Europe growing, think-tank warns
item.description: The risk of a small Russian nuclear strike in Europe is rising as the US military deterrent wanes, a British think-tank has warned.

item.title: How the Kremlin turns schoolchildren into future soldiers in occupied Ukraine
item.description: When Russian forces occupy a Ukrainian town, schools are often targeted first. An investigation into hundreds of Telegram posts from Russian propaganda channels operating in occupied Ukraine since 2022 reveals a systematic campaign to militarise and indoctrinate children through schools.

item.title: Fear, power politics and migration: whatever happened to Germany’s ‘welcome culture’?
item.description: Ten years ago, Germany symbolised Europe’s 'Willkommenskultur' (Welcome Culture). Chancellor Angela Merkel’s decision to open borders to refugees in 2015 was framed as a moral and historical responsibility. What has happened since?

item.title: Listen: Spain wants to regularise half a million undocumented migrants, in full contrast with European migration policies
item.description: Spain wants to regularise half a million undocumented migrants. Meanwhile, the rest of Europe is busy toughening migration rules. Is Spain the very last country on the continent to have a positive message around migration?

item.title: Leaked EU paper envisions dumping migrant sea rescues onto non-European states
item.description: The EU has been mulling sending people rescued in the Mediterranean directly to coastal states outside of Europe, according to an internal EU document.

item.title: 73 days to election: Roma people are for ‘cleaning shit-filled toilets’, says Hungarian minister
item.description: Our ongoing week-by-week debrief by award-winning journalist Veronika Munk, explaining the most important political developments in Hungary in the run-up to the crunch April election.

item.title: Far-right MEP tries to silence EUobserver over election-monitoring ban
item.description: French far-right MEP Virginie Joron claimed she was never punished for rogue election monitoring, but the EU Parliament confirmed she was lying, amid a wider crackdown.

item.title: The EU-India trade deal: ‘mother of deals’ or ‘overhyped’ and full of loopholes? The answer may be both
item.description: Why the EU-India trade deal sparks both praise and pushback — explained.

item.title: Iran ‘terrorist’ label does not signify backing for US strikes, EU says
item.description: Europe's designation of Iran's main army branch as “terrorists” on Thursday is not an endorsement of US military strikes, the EU's top diplomat has said.
